feedback.problem: Find the $x$-coordinates of the points where the circle $(x+1)^{2}+(y+1)^{2}=1$ intersects the line $y=-3x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find $x$-coordinates of the intersection points, we need to substitute $y=-3x$ into the equation of the circle and solve the resulting equation for $x,$ if possible:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2}+(y+1)^{2} & =1 \\ (x+1)^{2}+(-3x+1)^{2} & =1 \\ {x}^{2}+2x+1+9{x}^{2}-6x+1 & =1 \\ 10{x}^{2}-4x+1 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we compute the discriminant $D$ of the above quadratic equation, then we get

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =(-4)^{2}-4\cdot 10\cdot 1 \\  & =16-40 \\  & =-24.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $D=-24<0$, there are no real solutions to the equation $10{x}^{2}-4x+1=0.$

Therefore, we conclude that the circle $(x+1)^{2}+(y+1)^{2}=1$ does not intersect the line $y=-3x.$
